text: 20% in those aged 50 to 69 at diagnosis (too few women over 70 were given chemotherapy to esti- mate benefit in this group) • this survival advantage occurs largely independent of oestrogen receptor (ER) status, nodal status, or other tu- mour characteristics • adjuvant regimens including an anthracycline are more effective than those without a drug of this class • in women with ER-positive disease, about 5 years of treatment with adjuvant tamoxifen reduces the annual death rate due to breast cancer by around 31%, largely independent of age, other tumour characteristics, or the use of chemotherapy • combined chemotherapy and tamoxifen therefore in- creases the survival benefit further: for middle-aged women with ER-positive disease the breast-cancer mor- tality rate over 15 years would be approximately halved by 6 months of anthracycline-based chemotherapy fol- lowed by 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen • ovarian ablation (by surgery or irradiation) or ovarian suppression with a gonadorelin analogue also appear to reduce the mortality due to breast cancer, but that the advantage only applies where other adjuvant therapies are not given Although these data help in making therapeutic decisions, the size of the benefit will always be less in patients with good prognosis; in the most favourable cases (small tu- mours with no involved nodes) the incremental benefit may be too small to warrant adjuvant treatment.3 Tailoring systemic adjuvant therapy to the patient is important, and age and clinical characteristics alone are not adequate grounds to make the judgement: appropriate prognostic markers should be considered.19,20 The large analyses have led to the widespread adoption of anthracycline-based regimens for adjuvant chemotherapy, replacing earlier historical regimens such as CMF (cyclo- phosphamide, methotrexate, and fluorouracil) with those such as FAC or CAF (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, fluorouracil), AC (doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide), and their many variants. However, they do not take ac- count of more recent developments in molecular profiling of the tumour, nor of newer drugs that have become avail- able for adjuvant therapy. The EBCTCG analysis could not show any difference in effectiveness between anthracycline regimens,18 but regi- mens based on epirubicin have gained in popularity in many centres, since its lower cardiotoxicity compared with doxorubicin means that higher doses can be given. Addition of a taxane (docetaxel or paclitaxel) to an anthra- cycline-based regimen appears to improve disease-free and overall survival.21,22 There is evidence that HER2-re- ceptor status is prognostic for response to anthracycline- based regimens.3 There is also increasing interest in the early use of trastuzumab in women with HER2-overex- pressing tumours.
